<h1 align="center">Castaway</h1>

<p align="center">
  <b>A ten-hour lo-fi island video in which very little happens, on purpose.</b>
</p>

<p align="center">
  One young woman, one tiny island, one tall palm, one raft and a great deal of time. She idles, nodding to the music on her headphones, and every so often something happens: a message in a bottle washes straight back, a delivery drone brings a parcel that turns out to be more headphones, a coconut lands on a hermit crab and walks off with the crab inside. Every gag starts on the next bar of the music, so it lands on the beat. The tide supplies most of it. The tide also takes it back.
</p>

<p align="center">
  <sub>An unofficial remake, inspired by the small-island routines and visual comedy of <i>Johnny Castaway</i>, the 1992 desert-island screensaver, and not affiliated with it or its owners. Sunny, hand-painted coastal anime, 16:9, 1080p, 30 fps, and always daytime. Every sound is synthesized from code.</sub>
</p>

```sh
python tools/serve.py     # live preview, and export to a YouTube-ready MP4
# then open http://127.0.0.1:8765/
```

<details>
<summary><b>THE MANIFEST</b>: everything that turns up, and how it leaves</summary>

<br>

| Arrives | How | Leaves |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A message in a bottle | She sends it | Straight back, on the tide. A reply turns up later, in a different bottle. |
| A parcel | A delivery drone | Opened. Contents: another pair of headphones. |
| A grey tabby with a white chest | On a crate | Climbs the palm, naps, and one day floats away again. Comes back another time. |
| A sea turtle | Visits | In its own time. |
| A shark in headphones | Turns up | Not before nodding along to the beat. |
| A coconut | Falls on a hermit crab | Walks off, with the crab wearing it. |
| A sandcastle | She builds it | The tide. |
| A tour boat of selfie-takers | The sea | The sea. |
| A bro on an electric hydrofoil | Waves with a shaka | Carves off. |
| One bar of signal | Top of the palm only | The moment she climbs down. |
| A kumara | She plants it | It doesn't. It grows over the video. |
| An iced coffee | She walks out over the water and comes back with it | She could leave any time, you know. |
| A ship | The horizon | The horizon, while she is busy with a coconut. It waits for her to get busy. |

In between: coconut sipping, fishing, jogging laps, waving for rescue, and bushcraft (fire by friction, a hammock, a lookout up the palm, spear fishing).

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE SCHEDULE</b>: four timers, and every one of them lands on the bar</summary>

<br>

[activities.toml](activities.toml) holds more than 90 activities (94 when this header was made on 2026-10-01: 81 on four timers and 13 chained follow-ups), and grows every few hours.

| Timer | Comes round every | In a typical 10-hour run |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Regular | 2 to 5 minutes | about 155 |
| Occasional | 12 to 25 minutes | about 30 |
| Rare | 30 to 60 minutes | about 13 |
| Super rare | 3 to 6 hours, at most 3 a run | about 2 |

Typical means the median of 200 simulated runs, plus the chained follow-ups. She is busy about a third of the time and idles the rest. Lanes let things overlap, so a ship can sail past while she is busy with a coconut. Every activity waits for the next bar of the music (one every 3 seconds) before it starts. The default run is 10:00:00 with seed 1992.

The scene keeps itself busy too: 26 entries, 4 always-on effects and 22 timed events. Shore waves and drifting cloud shadows are built; distant birds, planes with vapour trails, whale pods, dolphins, sailboats, sandpipers, a gecko and a rain shower are planned.

```sh
python tools/schedule.py           # validate, then simulate a 10-hour run
python tools/render_demo.py --dev  # dev reel of every activity, with a HUD
```

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE SOUND</b>: made by code, all of it</summary>

<br>

- Every sound comes out of [tools/make_audio.py](tools/make_audio.py): no samples, no loops, no recordings, so no third-party licence applies. More than 150 sound files so far.
- The theme is a seamless 60-second loop at 80 BPM in F major, a ii-V-I-vi progression over 20 bars of exactly 3 seconds, with electric piano, a kalimba lead, soft drums and vinyl crackle. The ocean ambience is a seamless 60-second loop too.
- The mix sits at -14 LUFS, true peak at or below -1 dBTP. Levels are adjustable in master and per routine.
- Nobody has actually listened to any of it yet. The intro above is silent, which is at least consistent.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>THE MACHINE</b>: how a ten-hour video gets made</summary>

<br>

```text
 RENDERER ..... web/index.html, plain ES modules, no build step
 SERVER ....... tools/serve.py on 127.0.0.1:8765
 PREVIEW ...... live, in the browser
 VIDEO ........ WebCodecs H.264 in the browser, frame-exact
 SPEED ........ 68 to 78 frames a second at 1080p30 in Chrome
 SOUND ........ mixed by the server and joined to the video as one MP4
 NPM .......... no packages
 MOTION ....... hard cuts and stepped movement
 NIGHTS ....... none
```

The web page is the renderer. [tools/render_demo.py](tools/render_demo.py) is the older Python reference renderer, kept for its dev reel.

</details>

<details>
<summary><b>ABOUT THIS INTRO</b>: how the banner is made</summary>

<br>

The banner borrows the layout of a framed Amiga intro from around 1990-91: on black, a short grey strip holding a small logo plate, then a tall navy panel where the text itself carries the colour, three lines of wide slanted capitals filled with one rainbow. Its text page is the other half of the style: dense 8-pixel capitals in blocks tinted magenta, white, orange and light blue. Where those pages once said who supplied the release, this one says the tide did. The two windows in the grey strip are this banner's own addition.

- **Rainbow lines.** Each capital is drawn from a stroke skeleton with an elliptical pen, so the letters come out round, then slanted a pixel every four rows. All of them share one hard-stepped gradient across the panel, 48 twelve-bit colours, which moves one step every quarter second: colour cycling.
- **Pages.** Eight pages of three lines, two bars each (6 seconds at 80 BPM), 48 seconds a loop. Letters bob one pixel at a time on a wave that takes a bar, and fold away and back left to right when the page changes. Page one is in place on the first frame.
- **The plate.** A capsule with a three-pixel chrome rim, red capitals shaded row by row with white top edges, and a glint every two bars.
- **The windows.** She and the shark nod on every beat.
- **Calm.** Nothing large flashes; the fastest change is the colour cycle, one neighbouring hue at a time. With reduced motion switched on, everything holds on page one with the rainbow still.

No group's logo, letterforms or wording were copied: both fonts, the plate lettering, the sprites and every word are new. The Palm Readers are invented. Rebuild both images with `node src/31-amiga-logo-plate-intro_opus_5.5.mjs`.

</details>
